turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?
turns.patient_response:
Well, I came in because I just feel like I absolutely cannot get my schoolwork and my little accessories shop organized at the same time. I run this tiny shop online—I make these resin keychains and hair clips, which are super fun to do, but resin is honestly so finicky. Like, if the room isn't the exact right temperature, it gets all cloudy and ruins the whole batch. My roommate left the window open last week and I lost like ten pieces, which was so frustrating because resin is expensive... 

But anyway, yeah, between the shop and my classes, my supplies, due dates, receipts, and assignment notes all just end up in these massive piles all over my desk and floor. I stare at them and I just don't know what to do first. Like yesterday, I found a receipt for jump rings stuck inside my history notebook, which actually reminded me I still need to return this bulk pack of glitter to the craft store because it was totally the wrong shade of pink... but yeah, I just don't know where to start with any of my piles.

symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient explicitly states they cannot get their schoolwork and shop organized, describing massive piles of supplies and notes and not knowing what to do first.

turns.doctor_question: Have you struggled with organization and staying focused since you were a child, or is this a more recent problem?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, definitely since I was a kid. Like, my mom actually still has all these old notes from my elementary school teachers saved in this giant plastic bin in her garage. Which, by the way, I keep telling her she needs to organize because she just throws everything in there—like my old tap shoes are in the exact same box as my report cards, and it just makes absolutely no sense. I tried to help her sort it out over the holidays, but I ended up just sitting on the floor looking at all my old art projects for three hours. 

But anyway, yeah, if you look at the notes in that bin, they basically all say the exact same thing. The teachers were always telling my mom that I was constantly out of my seat, or complaining that I'd just start talking way before they even called on me. And I'd always rush through all our group activities, even when I totally understood the work. I just wanted to get to the next thing, you know? I remember this one time we were making these little dioramas out of shoeboxes, and I finished mine so fast I started trying to glue my friend's little plastic trees down for her because she was taking too long... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, if it was a recent problem. So yeah, definitely not a new thing at all.

symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient confirms the doctor's question about struggling with organization since childhood ('definitely since I was a kid').
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient demonstrates distractibility by losing track of the doctor's question mid-response and getting sidetracked by old art projects while trying to organize.
symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient recalls elementary school teachers noting that they were 'constantly out of my seat'.
symptom_reasoning.S016: The patient mentions teachers complaining that they would 'start talking way before they even called on me'.
symptom_reasoning.S018: The patient describes intruding on a friend's activity by taking over and gluing her project because she was taking too long.

turns.doctor_question: Nowadays, do you often feel physically restless or have trouble sitting still?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, absolutely. It's like... even when I don't actually have anywhere to go, I just feel like my body is constantly buzzing and I need to be moving. It's the absolute worst when I'm supposed to just sit still and listen, like in my classes. 

We have these terrible wooden seats in my Tuesday morning seminar, and they squeak so loud. I swear the girl next to me was giving me death glares last week because I kept bouncing my leg and shifting around, and the chair was just screeching the whole time. She had this really cool laptop sticker, though—it was from that volleyball anime? Haikyuu! Yeah, I actually thought about making some custom resin keychains inspired by it, like little volleyballs with orange glitter. But finding the exact right shade of orange glitter is surprisingly impossible. Most of them look way too neon, or like, super Halloween-y, you know? I bought three different jars on Amazon and had to return all of them because they just looked cheap when I mixed them into the resin... wait. What were we talking about? Oh, sitting still. But yeah, I just always have that buzzing feeling inside me.

symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient explicitly states they feel their body is constantly buzzing and they have a persistent need to be moving.
symptom_reasoning.S010: The patient describes bouncing their leg and shifting around in their seat during class.
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient demonstrates distractibility by getting sidetracked by thoughts of a laptop sticker and resin keychains, completely losing their train of thought.

turns.doctor_question: Have there ever been periods lasting several days where you felt full of energy and barely needed any sleep?
turns.patient_response:
No, I don't think so. I mean, I definitely have nights where I stay up super late because I'm just hyper-focused on finishing a batch of keychains. Like, once I start pouring the resin, I can't really stop, or it cures weirdly. But I'm always exhausted the next day. I totally need my sleep. 

Actually, speaking of sleep, my roommate got this new weighted blanket that she swears by, and she let me try it the other day. It was so heavy! Like, I felt like I was being squished into the mattress. It's supposed to help with anxiety or something, but I honestly just felt trapped. Plus, it was this awful beige color that totally clashed with everything in our room. I told her we should at least get a duvet cover for it—maybe something with a cute floral pattern, or even just a nice sage green. Sage green is so popular right now. I was actually thinking of doing a whole sage green collection for my shop, maybe with some little gold flakes mixed in... wait, sorry. What did you ask me about? Oh, sleep. Yeah, no, I definitely need my sleep. I've never had days where I just don't need it.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient gets distracted by her own unrelated thoughts about a weighted blanket and resin colors, causing her to lose her train of thought and forget the doctor's question.
symptom_reasoning.S015: The patient goes on a long, rambling, and unprompted tangent about her roommate's blanket, its color, and her shop's inventory.
symptom_reasoning.S034: The patient denies having periods lasting several days where she feels full of energy, noting she is always exhausted after staying up late.
symptom_reasoning.S036: The patient explicitly states she totally needs her sleep and has never had days where she doesn't need it.

turns.patient_response:
Yeah, all the time. It's actually super embarrassing. Like, whenever we have group critiques in my art classes, or even just regular discussions, I just... I jump right in with my answer before the other person is even done talking. It's like my brain just automatically guesses what they're going to say, and I can't hold it in. And then half the time, I'm wrong about what they were going to say anyway! 

Which reminds me, last week in critique, this guy was talking about his charcoal piece, and I totally interrupted him because I thought he was going to say he struggled with the shading on the left side, but he was actually talking about the paper texture. And speaking of paper texture, I just bought this amazing new mixed-media sketchbook. The paper is so thick, you can practically use watercolors on it without it warping. I've been trying to get more into watercolor lately, but honestly, it's so hard to control. The water just goes everywhere. I bought these tiny little detail brushes to help, but they were so expensive. Art supplies are ridiculously priced, aren't they? I swear I spend half my budget at Michaels. They have good coupons, though, if you use their app... wait. I'm doing it again, aren't I? What was the question? Oh, blurting things out. Yeah, I definitely do that a lot. It's really frustrating.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient demonstrates being easily distracted by unrelated thoughts, going on a tangent about art supplies and forgetting the original question.
symptom_reasoning.S016: The patient explicitly confirms jumping in with answers before the other person is done talking.
